notCaptured.reason: No design-system implementation of the proposed variant exists yet; rendering one now would be implementation before approval. The captures show the Foundation and web sources only.

The approved v0.2 appearance is unchanged by this amendment and already covered by the v0.1 expected-design reference VIS-01 (docs/design/foundation-boards/v2026-10-17/Link.png, sha256 31eb1841a9bc072f49c5aaf2e7fa3fa4d2dbd3077eb5bccb146c827f93e7b03f); it was not re-captured.

limits: The captures show the Foundation and web .eg-link/.link appearance: 15px/600 labels, 18px arrows, 1px brand underline and a 2px bottom inset. They are evidence for the web treatment and its roles, not approved expected design for the design-system recipe (which uses text-label-default and 16px icons).
The preview harness loaded only the font weights the rows use; heavier Barlow and Barlow Condensed weights are unfetched, so the captures cannot validate those weights.
pulso-source.html is a template with Jinja image placeholders and an external Google Fonts request; the link crops do not depend on either, and the loaded families are recorded above.

The web arrows carry no aria-hidden in the source (a real web accessibility defect); the captures therefore document the web defect as evidence, not as expected behavior for the design-system component.
Only one web external anchor sets target/rel in the capture set, and it ships rel="noopener" without noreferrer; the design-system component keeps its stricter merged rel.
Browser images do not verify behavior, accessibility, keyboard, focus or contrast.

A localized difference in PNG bytes can appear between runs of the same script (scroll-dependent compositing); the hashes above are of the files stored in this folder and must be re-verified with sha256sum before linking them in any published comment.

approval.reference: Pending: the owner approves or declines these captures as supporting evidence for Link v0.3 in issue #61. The captures are source evidence and grant no expected-design approval.
